sentences.text:
Mr.P.Muthukumar, learned State Government Pleader for respondents 1 to 6; and,
Mr.Su.Srinivasan, learned counsel for respondents 7 and 8.
2.

The appellant has filed a writ petition challenging the notification issued under Section 3A(1) of the National Highways Act, 1956 seeking to acquire the land of the appellant comprised in Survey No.22/5A.
In the writ petition, the appellant filed two applications  one seeking interim injunction and the other for appointment of an independent surveyor.
Both the applications are rejected.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that a major chunk of the appellant's land was acquired in the past acquisition.
The said land is not put to use by the respondents and now notification is i s s u e d i n r e s p e c t o f t h e l e f t o v e r l a n d o f t h e a p p e l l a n t .
_ _ _ _ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.A.Nos.65 and 63 of 2024
The left over land of the appellant is the only to an extent of 808 Sq.Mtrs.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the alignment has been wrongly made by the respondents.
The property in question is the only property left with the appellant.
The appellant has spent a huge amount and has erected a water plant on the subject land.
Learned counsel submits that the writ petition is still pending and at least till the pendency of the writ petition, the respondents be injuncted from taking the possession.
4. The land is required for the highway.
The same is a public cause.
It has been observed that even award under Section 3G of the Act has been passed in May, 2023.
The award does not seem to have been challenged in the writ petition.
5. As far as the alignment is concerned, the same is the job of the experts.
The courts cannot substitute its decision over the decision of the experts with regard to the alignment of the highway.
6. The amount is also determined.

It is submitted by learned ____________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.A.Nos.65 and 63 of 2024 State Government Pleader and learned counsel for the National Highways Authority of India that the said amount has been deposited.
The appellant can withdraw the said amount at any point of time.
7. The appellant also would have the right to approach the arbitrator for enhancement of compensation.
At this stage, it would not be appropriate to pass interim orders.
8. The appellant may request the learned Single Judge to decide the writ petition expeditiously.
The writ appeals are disposed of accordingly.
There shall be no order as to costs.

Consequently,
C.M.P.Nos.383, 381 and 387 of 2024 are closed.
(S.V.G., CJ.)
